title: Minimum supervisory ratios for pharmacy support personnel
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a) a pharmacist using interns, certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees to assist in filling prescriptions may supervise a maximum of four support personnel only if at least one of the four is a certified pharmacy technician and one is a pharmacy intern, or at least two are certified pharmacy technicians, or two are pharmacy interns; otherwise the maximum is three support personnel and at least one of the three must be a pharmacy intern or a certified pharmacy technician. Under 247 CMR 8.06(3)(b) sales clerks, messengers, delivery personnel, secretaries and other persons outside those definitions are excluded from the ratio so long as they are not supporting the pharmacist in any professional capacity.
exam_relevance: Tests the composition conditions that unlock a four-to-one ratio rather than a flat headcount, and which staff are excluded from the count entirely.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.conditions: only when the credential composition conditions in 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a)1 are met

numeric_facts.fact: default maximum support personnel per pharmacist
numeric_facts.conditions: at least one must be a pharmacy intern or certified pharmacy technician

common_confusions: A four-to-one ratio is not available on headcount alone; the credential mix is the condition.
Non-professional staff are excluded from the ratio, not counted as a fourth support person.
verification_notes: Read in the current official Board of Registration in Pharmacy publication of 247 CMR 8.00 on 2026-08-19 during Batch 3 tranche B3-A authoring under Issue #91. A fresh independent legal and full-bank realism audit is still required before release.
